## Why This Question Is Asked
This evaluates understanding of data isolation in shared ML infrastructure, origin-bound access tokens, rapid incident response for cross-tenant data leakage, and practical tooling decisions for enterprise-grade security.

## Key Concepts
- Tenant isolation in feature stores and vector databases
- Fine-grained IAM with attribute-based access control (ABAC)
- API gateway runtime validation using policy engines (OPA/Rego)
- Envelope encryption with customer-managed KMS keys
- Audit trails, data lineage, and compliance logging
- Incident response playbook with containment, eradication, and recovery phases

## Code Example
```rego
package policy.tenant_isolation

default allow = false

allow {
    input.tenant == data.tenants[input.tenant_id].owner
    input.action == "read"
    input.resource_namespace == input.tenant_id
    not exceeds_quota(input.tenant_id, input.request_size)
}

allow {
    input.tenant == data.tenants[input.tenant_id].owner
    input.action == "write"
    input.resource_namespace == input.tenant_id
    input.token_expires_at > time.now_ns()
}

exceeds_quota(tenant_id, size) {
    data.tenants[tenant_id].quota_used + size > data.tenants[tenant_id].quota_limit
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you validate tenant boundaries without introducing significant latency at inference time?
- What monitoring alerts would trigger automatic containment actions?
- How do you handle key rotation for envelope encryption without downtime?

## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates practical security controls for serverless applications and secrets management at a beginner level, focusing on tangible implementation steps and measurable success criteria.

- **Least-privilege IAM roles**: Grant only the permissions required for each Lambda function to operate

- Secrets rotate automatically per defined schedule
- CI pipeline blocks all commits containing detected secrets
- Incident response playbook is documented, tested quarterly, and accessible to on-call personnel

## Why This Is Asked
Tests SecOps of supply-chain risk and rapid containment in multi-tenant SaaS.

## Key Concepts
- Supply-chain security, SBOM, reproducible builds, attestation, canary deployment, rapid rollback.
- CI/CD hardening with Dependabot, SBOM scanning, and signed artifacts.
- Incident metrics: MTTR, RPO, RTO, blast radius.

## Code Example
```javascript
name: Build and attest
on: [push]
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Build
        run: npm ci && npm run build
      - name: SBOM
        run: syft packages dir:./dist -o cyclonedx | tee bom.xml
      - name: Sign
        run: cosign sign --key cosign.key ./dist
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you verify all tenants are protected during rollout and when to roll back?
- What if a compromised CI runner existed?
